Tawazon - A massive fire tore through a coastal community in the southern Philippines late on Tuesday night, destroying around 1,000 homes and displacing thousands of residents on a small islet in Barangay Lamion, Bongao, in the Tawi-Tawi province of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region.

The blaze, believed to have started at about 10 p.m. local time, quickly spread through the densely packed village as strong winds and the flammable materials used in many stilt houses fueled the inferno.

फिलिपाईन्समधील एका छोट्या बेटावर लागलेल्या भीषण आगीने प्रचंड हाहाकार माजवला असून हजारो लोक रस्त्यावर आले आहेत. सरकारी वृत्तसंस्था 'PNA' ने दिलेल्या माहितीनुसार, ही आग रात्री १० च्या सुमारास'बारंगाय लामियन' परिसरात लागली. या आगीत तब्बल १,००० घरं पूर्णपणे जळून राख झाली आहेत. वेगवान वाऱ्यामुळे आगीने रौद्ररूप धारण केलं आणि दाट लोकवस्तीच्या परिसरात एकच खळबळ उडाली.

या आगीने संपूर्ण परिसरात मोठं नुकसान झालं आहे. PNA नुसार, या दुर्घटनेनंतर ५,००० हून अधिक लोकांना जमीन आणि समुद्र अशा दोन्ही मार्गांनी सुरक्षित बाहेर काढण्यात आलं आहे. सध्या या विस्थापित नागरिकांना दोन तात्पुरत्या मदत छावण्यांमध्ये ठेवण्यात आले आहे.

data.text:
Ever catch yourself staring out the window in the UK, pension day arrives, and it's just… more rain and the same four walls?

Feels like the “golden years” got lost in the post-divorce fog, right?

I keep hearing from British lads in their 50s and 60s who finally said sod it and moved to the Philippines. 

They tell me the monotony vanished almost overnight.

You wake up to actual sunshine, roosters going mental, mangoes that taste like they shouldn't be legal.

Instead of debating whether to risk a damp walk, you're deciding beach or boat today. San Miguel in hand at sunset. Proper colours in the sky for once.

The money side helps a ton — pension goes stupidly far. Decent place near the water for what you'd pay for a shoebox in Birmingham. 

Eat out every night, maybe get a cleaner or driver if you fancy it. No guilt.

Then there's the actual doing stuff:
snorkelling with turtles
chasing waterfalls
playing golf that doesn't cost a mortgage
hopping between islands that look photoshopped

Blokes who've done it say the same thing: “I was just existing back home. Here I feel alive again.” 

Warm locals, English spoken everywhere, expat groups full of other Brits doing exactly what you're thinking about.

Sure, there's downsides. Manila traffic will test your soul.

Paperwork happens on “Filipino time.” You need a decent sense of humour. 

But escaping the grey routine? For a lot of guys, it's been the best call they ever made.

If you're fed up with the same old script, maybe it's time to try a tropical rewrite. 🌴

Anyone else daydreaming about ditching the drizzle? Drop a 🇵🇭 if the Philippines just popped onto your list. Or tell me straight — what's the one thing still holding you back? 👇

ICYMI O/N

A renewed bout of silver (-10%) liquidiations put pressure on broader commodities (BCOM -0.6%) and risk appetite during the APAC session while crypto made new lows (BTC 70k). US futures (NQ +0.3%, ES +0.1%) are marginally off Wednesday's lows, coming off the back of tech's worst period since last April, failing so far to benefit from Alphabet's (-1%) mega capex guide with Qualcomm (-11%) and Arm (-7%) also hit post-earnings with both feeling the pain of the memory shortage; attention moving now to Amazon (flat YTD) after market close on Thursday. Asian indices were all largely lower, extending the momentum led sell-off from the US session on Wednesday, with the memory-levered Kospi (-3.9%) the underperformer; note reports HP, Dell, and Acer are sounding out Chinese memory producers. DXY and USTs are little changed ahead of the delayed JOLTS data released. JGBs (30yy -8bps) outperforming after a solid 30yr auction eased concerns ahead of an expected Takaichi sweep; yen little changed. BoE and ECB rate decisions coming up, both expected to stand pat. Note the Pound (EURGBP +0.3%) and Gilts (30yy +3bps) are underperforming as pressure on PM Starmer ramps up. 

MACRO:

Silver fell sharply, wiping out a two-day recovery, as the white metal struggled to find a floor following a historic market rout. Gold also declined. (BBG)

'Kevin Warsh channels Alan Greenspan in AI productivity bet' FT article highlights recent Warsh comments that argue for lower rates as the AI boom is boosting productivity. (FT)

Arm boss Rene Haas has said fears about AI hurting software companies, which triggered a market sell-off this week, are a “micro-hysteria” that exceeds the reality of how businesses are using the tools. (FT)

Democrats’ drive to reach a deal to put new restrictions on immigration-enforcement agents is running into a Republican brick wall, with lawmakers in both parties saying an agreement looks increasingly unlikely by a Feb. 13 deadline. (WSJ)

Top Senate negotiators said an effort to renew expired healthcare subsidies had effectively collapsed, likely ending the hopes of 20 million Americans that the tax-credit expansion could be revived and lower their monthly insurance premiums. (WSJ)

The top Democrat on a House committee overseeing U.S.-China competition has launched an investigation into a $500 million investment by an Abu Dhabi royal in a Trump family cryptocurrency company and is urging a U.S. attorney to probe the deal as well. (WSJ)

Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook sees a greater threat to the economy from elevated inflation than from a weakening labor market, a stance that suggests she could be skeptical of supporting a return to rate cuts. (WSJ)

Extreme market swings from metals to currencies are fueling a hiring push at hedge funds and banks as they seek traders who can capitalize on surging volatility. (BBG)

Longer-dated Japanese government bonds rose on Thursday following solid demand at a closely watched auction of 30-year debt, even as a crucial election loomed on Sunday that would shape the government's big fiscal stimulus plans. (RTRS)

Japan must avoid ramping up fiscal spending in a way that fuels inflation and forces the central bank to raise interest rates rapidly, Toshihiro Nagahama, a government panel member known as an economic aide to premier Sanae Takaichi, said on Thursday. (RTRS)

Investors may return to longer-dated Japanese debt after this weekend’s snap election, with big asset managers pinpointing 10-year yields reaching 2.5% as a possible trigger to buy, according to a Mizuho strategist. (BBG)

The yen is on track for its biggest weekly drop since October, as traders brace for a decisive victory by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s Liberal Democratic Party in this weekend’s election. (BBG)

Stock investors are positioning for a decisive election victory by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi this Sunday, betting that a strong mandate will allow her to consolidate power and push through expansive fiscal policies. (BBG)

Most Chinese provinces are targeting lower economic growth this year, in what many economists believe is a signal Beijing will set a historically low range of 4.5-5 per cent for its official goal in 2026. Of the 29 out of China’s 31 province-level areas that have so far announced growth targets, 19 have cut them compared with 2025, according to a tally by the FT. (FT)

Chinese stocks are encountering a fresh hurdle as Beijing ramps up efforts to collect corporate taxes, a move that threatens to pressure earnings in a fragile economy. (BBG)

Chinese consumer stocks are winning favor with investors just as their high-flying tech peers lose ground amid a global rout, with expectations growing that the former will benefit from increased spending during the upcoming Lunar New Year break. (BBG)

New data on China’s relentless energy installations underscore warnings from Elon Musk and Jensen Huang that the nation’s world-beating power network will deliver a major advantage over the US in the race to dominate artificial intelligence. (BBG)

Analysts expect reserve requirement ratio cuts to be unlikely ahead of the mid‑February Spring Festival, though implementation could be possible in the second quarter, according to a Securities Daily report Thursday. (Securities Daily)

New filings for private manager‑of‑managers (MOM) fund products in China have been suspended in recent months amid regulatory concerns that the business could devolve into a mere “channel” operation, potentially increasing investment risks. (Securities Times)

The European Central Bank is set to hold interest rates steady for a fifth meeting, judging that the latest bout of global tensions and euro strength haven’t thrown the economy off course yet. (BBG)

German manufacturing orders unexpectedly jumped in December, a sign that the recent struggles of the country’s industrial sector might be fading as Berlin’s fiscal stimulus ramps up. (WSJ)

The Bank of England is expected to keep interest rates on hold on Thursday and leave its options open about when it will cut them again as it waits to be sure that a weakening jobs market will push down on inflation pressures. (RTRS)

Anger is growing among Keir Starmer's own Labour MPs over his handling of the Peter Mandelson scandal. Polymarket odds of Starmer out by year-end have risen to 65% from 55% over the past day. (BBC/Polymarket)

The yield gap between two- and 10-year gilts hit the widest since 2018 as a fresh round of UK political turbulence weighed on government bonds. (BBG)

The Australian dollar’s outlook is increasingly at risk as a slide in precious metals works against optimism driven by expectations for higher interest rates. (BBG)

The Reserve Bank of Australia may be forced to raise interest rates for a second consecutive time in March, according to Westpac Banking Corp. Chief Economist Luci Ellis, as the central bank embarks on the world’s first tightening cycle of 2026. (BBG)

Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers faced criticism after his opposition counterpart urged him to apologize to economist Diana Mousina for “misrepresenting” her remarks about the government’s role in reviving inflation and, in turn, the first interest-rate hike of 2026. (BBG)

Australia’s trade minister is set to travel to Brussels for talks with European Union officials to try and secure a free trade accord, which if signed would be the bloc’s third major agreement this year and bolster its efforts to stave off pressure from the Trump administration. (BBG)

Czech policymakers are set to hold interest rates at their first meeting of 2026 as an expected slowdown in headline inflation may open room for more monetary easing this year. (BBG)

The Hong Kong dollar drifted down to near the weakest level since August as excess cash in the banking system spurred carry trade bets against the pegged currency. (BBG)

South Korea is seeking closer cooperation with China on critical mineral supply chains, its trade ministry said on Thursday, as Seoul unveiled plans to secure stable supplies of rare earths needed for cutting-edge technologies. (RTRS)

Seoul apartment prices extended a rally that is testing the government’s efforts to curb speculative buying and sharpening President Lee Jae Myung’s criticism of those who own more than one home. (BBG)

'Why Big Tech Is Throwing Cash Into India in Quest for AI Supremacy' WSJ article profiles India's favourable tax treatment for tech investments, highlighting the tens of billions pledged by US big tech names in Indian data center investments. (WSJ)

Taiwan will increase its purchases of U.S. natural gas and reduce purchases from other countries, Taiwan Economy Minister Kung Ming-hsin said on Thursday. (RTRS)

Taiwan’s AI Boom Is Minting Millionaires, Stoking Inequality. (BBG)

South Africa’s development finance institution has invested $20 million in a domestic rare earths project, which aims to help the European Union reduce its dependence on China for critical minerals. (BBG)

Indonesia’s economic growth surged to a three-year high as state stimulus buoyed demand, potentially boosting sentiment after a recent slump in the rupiah and local stocks. (BBG)

China’s coal importers are ready to turn to alternative supplies if Indonesia’s lower production quotas curb exports, a shift that could undermine Jakarta’s efforts to lift prices and risk alienating its top buyer. (BBG)

The Malaysian ringgit, Asia’s top performing currency in the past year, still has potential to gain as the economy continues to perform strongly, Second Finance Minister Amir Hamzah Azizan said, indicating that growth forecasts may be revised higher. (BBG)

Thailand’s headline inflation remained in the negative territory for a 10th straight month, extending the country’s longest stretch of falling prices since the pandemic. (BBG)

Philippine inflation accelerated to the highest in nearly a year, and returned within the central bank’s target as monetary authorities reaffirmed that the easing cycle may be drawing to a close. (BBG)

Interest-rate swap transactions in the Philippines have jumped more than 60-fold since the launch of a peso IRS facility in late 2024, the nation’s central bank chief said, citing that a deepening market may improve the effectiveness of monetary policy. (BBG)

GEOPOLITICAL:

China is asking state firms to halt talks over new projects in Panama, as part of Beijing’s broader retaliation after the Central American country voided CK Hutchison Holdings Ltd.’s contract to operate two ports along its strategic canal, according to Bloomberg sources. (BBG)

China opposes any country undermining the international economic and trade order through rules imposed by small groups, the Chinese foreign ministry said on Thursday, after the United States unveiled plans for a preferential trade bloc of allies for critical minerals. (RTRS)

EQUITIES:

Alphabet saw choppy trade after it reported fourth-quarter revenue that beat expectations, with Google Cloud rising 48% Y/Y (exp. +36%) but said it planned to spend $175 billion to $185 billion this year, compared with the $119.5 billion analysts expected, lifting semiconductor stocks broadly in after hours trade. It reported Gemini monthly active users had reached 750mln (prev. 650mln last q) and said, "We’re seeing our AI investments and infrastructure drive revenue and growth across the board." (BBG/GOOGL)  

Qualcomm gave a lackluster revenue forecast for the current period, stoking concern that memory component shortages will hurt consumer demand by driving prices up. The shares dropped in extended trading. (BBG)

Reuters sources report the Trump administration is willing to allow China's ByteDance to buy Nvidia's H200 chips, but the AI chipmaker has not agreed to proposed conditions for their use. The government wants Know-Your-Customer (KYC) requirement as now drafted - to ensure China's military does not access the chips - among other conditions. (RTRS)

Arm Holdings Plc shares tumbled in late trading after the chip designer’s sales forecast disappointed investors, who have grown more skeptical of companies tied to artificial intelligence in recent days. (BBG)

Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which recently merged with xAI, has reached out to major index providers, including Nasdaq, to discuss how SpaceX and this year’s other hot startups might join key indexes sooner than normal ahead of its expected IPO later this year, according to WSJ sources. (WSJ)

PC makers HP, Dell, Acer and Asus are considering sourcing memory chips from Chinese chipmakers for the first time amid a global supply crunch that is threatening product launches and pushing up costs across the tech industry, Nikkei Asia reported on Thursday. (Nikkei)

Snap reported better-than-expected holiday quarter sales despite a decline in daily users, a sign of the continued evolution of its advertising business and its growing suite of consumer subscription services that are now contributing meaningfully to the company’s bottom line. (BBG)

Elf Beauty raised its annual sales and profit forecasts after beating Wall Street estimates for third-quarter results on Wednesday, as demand for its affordable cosmetics stayed strong despite rising economic and tariff uncertainty, sending shares up about 12% after the bell. (RTRS)

Analog chipmaker SiTime Corp. has agreed to acquire Renesas Electronics Corp.’s timing unit in a cash-and-stock transaction valued at about $2.9 billion. (BBG)

Baidu is set to pay its inaugural dividend this year and authorized a $5 billion share-buyback program, as part of the Beijing-based tech company’s broader capital-return strategy. (WSJ)

BYD is aiming to produce and source 50% of its vehicle components locally at its new Brazilian factory by the end of 2026, the company’s top executive in the country told Reuters, amid concerns about the EV giant undercutting the local industry. (RTRS)

Samsung to Expand DRAM Capacity for HBM4 by 120,000 Wafers per Month. (Hankyung via @jukan05)

Foxcon's revenue rose 35.5% in January, suggesting demand for Nvidia Corp. servers remains resilient during a global wave of AI development. (BBG)

TSMC plans to start making more-advanced chips in Japan, a move that would be a major boost to the country’s efforts to secure cutting-edge technology needed for artificial intelligence. (WSJ)

TSMC is poised to transform Chiayi, southern Taiwan into the world's largest advanced semiconductor packaging hub. Construction is expected to wrap up by 2031. (CTEE via @dnystedt)

ASE Technology Holding, the world's largest chip packaging and testing provider, on Thursday said it expects its leading-edge advanced packaging business to double in size to $3.2 billion in 2026. (RTRS)

Sony boosted its annual earnings guidance after reporting higher profit on the strength of its game, music and image-sensor businesses. Sony also said in January that it planned to set up a JV with Hong Kong-listed consumer electronics maker TCL Electronics Holdings, a move that would mark the end of majority ownership in its television business. (WSJ)

Nippon Steel is considering selling as much as 500 billion yen ($3.2 billion) of convertible bonds, according to Reuters sources, in a transaction that would be the largest of its kind in Japan. (RTRS)

Shell maintained its $3.5 billion quarterly buyback despite a fall in earnings as weaker prices weigh on oil major’s balance sheets. (WSJ)

Rio Tinto and Glencore are expected to announce an extension to merger talks ahead of a UK regulatory deadline on Thursday, to allow Rio more time to study the merits of any deal, according to Reuters sources. (RTRS)

Anglo American has warned of the prospect of a third writedown of the De Beers diamonds business it is trying to sell as it contends with a prolonged slump in the market for the precious stones. (FT)

Visma, the €19bn private equity-backed software group, may delay its plans for London’s biggest initial public offering in years after a broad sell-off in the sector. (FT)

HSBC Holdings Plc is preparing to hand some bankers little or zero bonuses as the 160-year-old British lender seeks to emulate its Wall Street rivals with a more hard-edged, “eat-what-you-kill” stance. (BBG)

Two Canadian pension giants plan to sell their stakes in Associated British Ports in a deal that they hope will value the UK’s biggest ports operator at more than £10bn. (FT)

Vodafone Group Plc grew more slowly than expected in Germany, its largest market, bucking expectations of stronger growth after bringing on 1&1 AG as a wholesale customer. (BBG)

BNP Paribas upgraded its midterm targets as it banks on cost-cutting and profit-boosting initiatives already under way to drive growth through 2028. (WSJ)

Siemens Healthineers said fiscal first-quarter revenue grew on a comparable basis as results in its core business units, imaging and precision therapy, offset currency and tariff challenges. Co. reaffirmed guidance. (WSJ)

ArcelorMittal said European measures to protect domestic steel production could boost its market share on the continent, as the company looks to arrest the decline in earnings booked last year. (WSJ)

Danske Bank said it would launch a new share buyback and pay out an increased dividend after earnings came in above guidance, driven by strength in core operations. (WSJ)

Sales of Novo Nordisk's blockbuster diabetes drug Ozempic in the greater China region fell for the first time last year, as it grapples with competition from rivals. (RTRS)

A.P. Moller-Maersk A/S said it will focus on cost discipline this year as the container giant faces deteriorating freight rates from the re-opening of the Red Sea. (BBG)

Volvo Cars' fourth-quarter profit fell 68%, hit by tariffs and weak demand, as the Sweden-based automaker warned on Thursday that external factors continued to pose challenges. (RTRS)

Spain's BBVA reported a rise in profit for the fourth quarter, driven by loan growth across its key markets and stable costs. (WSJ)

KEEP MOVING WITH MOVE IT

Built for people who don’t pause for traffic, Move It by Grab Philippines officially unveiled its new brand promise, “Keep Moving,” during a media launch held today at Cur8, Banilad Town Center.

“The Philippines now ranks as the most congested country in Asia. With MOVEIT, we believe it doesn’t have to be that way. That’s why tonight, we are introducing a new brand promise—to keep moving,” shared Rich Manuel, Move It’s Driver Engagement Lead. “This is built on three standards: keeping people moving reliably, keeping them moving safely, and keeping them moving with professionalism you can trust.”

The new brand promise reinforces Move It’s vision of mobility with purpose, designed to serve the daily grind of Filipinos on the move.

Sumentro sa pagbabayanihan bilang pagtugon sa baha ang naging mensahe ni Metropolitan Manila Development Authority Chairman Atty. Don Artes sa Oplan Kontra Baha Summit for Greater Metro Manila na pinangunahan ng Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) sa DPWH Central Office sa Manila ngayong araw.

Binigyang-diin ni Chairman Artes na ang pagtugon sa baha ay hindi lamang responsibilidad ng isang ahensiya, kundi ng buong bansa, pambansang pamahalaan, lokal na pamahalaan, pribadong sektor, at komunidad. “Ang tunay na pagbabago ay nakikita sa araw-araw na pagtupad sa responsibilidad at hindi lamang bilang tugon sa krisis.”

Ayon sa kaniya, ang bayanihan ay susi upang ang layuning ito ay maging hindi lamang ambisyon kundi isang kolektibong responsibilidad.

Ang Oplan Kontra Baha ay panawagan para sa pagkakaisa at kooperasyon ng lahat, hindi lang mga ahensiya at pribadong sektor ngunit pati rin ang mga mamamayang Pilipino. Target nitong maging flood-resilient ang Kalakhang Maynila sa pamamagitan ng tuloy-tuloy na pagtutulungan.

🚨Sanral Traffic Advisory🚨

Temporary Nighttime Road Closures On The M13 Offramp At Paradise Valley

The South African National Roads Agency SOC Limited (SANRAL) wishes to advise motorists of temporary nighttime road closures on the M13 Offramp at Paradise Valley for asphalt paving to accommodate jacking of the existing bridge vertically as part of the ongoing construction of the upgraded M13 Paradise Valley Off Ramp bridge over the N3 Highway.

Sanral appreciates the public’s patience and cooperation as it undertakes this vital project to alleviate long term traffic congestion in the area.

*The temporary road closures will take place as follows - N3 West Bound closure of M13 offramp at Paradise Valley (Exit 17 - N3 from Durban to M13 Pinetown/Kloof)*

• *Closures*
Each night from 20:00 to 04:30 from Thursday, 5 February 2026 to Wednesday, 18 February 2026. 

Traffic will remain on the N3 Westbound carriageway during this period. The M13 can be accessed via the M1 Richmond Road interchange.

Note that the M13 Eastbound onramp to the N3 (Pinetown to Durban) at Paradise Valley remains fully open.

As required for the safety of both road users and the construction team, full traffic accommodation plans are in place.

Trucks and heavy vehicles are advised to try and delay trips over this period, find suitable staging areas or reroute via the M13 or N3 to avoid major congestion. 

Public transport operators are asked to ensure their drivers are aware of route closures and alternatives affecting their commuter routes.

All road users are advised to plan their routes ahead of time and where possible leave for destinations earlier than usual.

*Closure Locations - N3 Off Ramp to the M13 at Paradise Valley (Exit 17)*

• N3 Off Ramp to the M13 fully closed at Paradise Valley (Exit 17).
• Traffic will be diverted to continue on the N3 Westbound Carriageway and join the M13 via the M1 Richmond Road.
• The M13 East bound onramp to the N3 (Pinetown to Durban) at Paradise Valley remains fully open.

“SANRAL appeals to road users to note and comply with the advance warning signs and speed restrictions when travelling through the construction work zones. To prioritise the safety of both the construction workers and road users, the speed limit along the route will be reduced during construction”
